Chapter 9: Living with Presence—Bringing Stillness into Action.
Most of us picture stillness as something that lives in quiet corners—maybe early mornings, silent retreats, or peaceful walks with no one else around. But what if real stillness isn’t about stepping away from the noise? What if it’s about showing up, fully present, in the middle of life’s everyday commotion?
Let me share a story. There was a nurse working those long, demanding shifts in a busy hospital. She often felt completely overwhelmed—barely finding a moment to eat, much less pause for herself. But she started something small. Before walking into a patient’s room, she’d take a deep breath. She’d notice the warmth of a hand, or quietly offer a blessing as she moved down the hallway. These moments didn’t slow her down, but they changed everything about her day. She became less reactive, more compassionate, and found she could truly connect with her patients—even amidst all the chaos.
See, a lot of us believe that presence only happens under perfect conditions. We think we need a quiet space, uninterrupted time, or a mind free from distractions. But the truth is, presence isn’t about your surroundings. It’s about how you show up, no matter what’s happening around you.
Here’s another example. Imagine a father, constantly juggling work and family. He felt guilty—a tug-of-war between his job and his kids. But one evening, while helping his daughter with her homework, he decided to make a simple change. He put away his phone and gave her his full attention. The conversation wasn’t remarkable, but the connection? That was real. In that moment, he realized presence wasn’t about having more time—it was about being fully where he was.
Living with presence is a practice. It’s a choice—to bring a little stillness into action, to notice your life as it unfolds, and to respond with openness and care. The nurse still had busy days, but her heart felt lighter. The father, just by paying attention, found his relationships deepening in ways he hadn’t expected.
So, what’s the takeaway here? Presence isn’t an escape from life. It’s a way to live more fully right in the middle of it.
